1.q: 6 children play rock-paper-scissors. Every child plays one game against each of the other children. How many games are played?
1.hint: Call the children A, B, C and so on. List the games that A plays, then the new games that B plays.
1.why: A plays 5 games. B has 4 new games, C has 3 new games, D has 2 new games and E has 1 new game. So 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 15 games.

1.q: Mei starts a school race in 19th place. There are 30 runners. She passes 5 runners. Then 2 runners pass her. What place is Mei in now? Write the number only.
1.hint: Passing runners moves Mei forward in the order. Being passed moves her back. Do the two steps one at a time.
1.why: Passing 5 runners moves Mei forward: 19 − 5 = 14. Then 2 runners pass her, so she moves back: 14 + 2 = 16.

1.q: Two scouts camp at the same campsite. Ravi camps from the 2nd to the 29th of the month. Dan camps from the 13th to the 30th. Each scout is there on his first and last day too. On how many days are both scouts at the campsite?
1.hint: Find the first day when both scouts are there, and the last day when both are there.
1.why: Both scouts are there from the 13th to the 29th. That is 29 − 13 + 1 = 17 days.

1.q: A secret 2-digit number has two clues. Its two digits add up to 9. Its tens digit is 3 more than its ones digit. What is the secret number?
1.hint: Try different ones digits. Which tens digit goes with each one?
1.why: The tens digit is 3 more than the ones digit. A ones digit of 3 gives a tens digit of 6, and 6 + 3 = 9. The number is 63.

1.q: A kopitiam sells 4 kinds of noodles and 5 kinds of drinks. A set is one noodle dish and one drink. How many different sets can you order?
1.hint: Pick one noodle dish. How many sets does it make with the drinks?
1.why: Each of the 4 noodle dishes goes with 5 drinks: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 sets.

1.q: Siti is 9 and her brother is 5. They both have a birthday once a year. After how many birthdays will the sum of their ages be 30?
1.hint: Add their ages now. At every birthday each of them gets one year older, so the sum grows by the same amount each time.
1.why: Now their ages add up to 9 + 5 = 14. At each birthday the sum grows by 2, because both get a year older. They need 30 − 14 = 16 more, and 16 ÷ 2 = 8 birthdays.

1.q: Dina plays a counting game. She starts at 6. She goes up 4, then down 1, then up 4, then down 1, and so on. Her first four numbers are 6, 10, 9, 13. What is her 11th number?
1.hint: Look at the going up and the going down together. They change the number by the same amount every time.
1.why: Going up 4 and down 1 makes the number 3 bigger each time. The 11th number comes after 10 steps, which is 5 pairs of steps: 6 + 5 × 3 = 21.

1.q: Uncle cuts a bamboo pole that is 36 cm long into 4 pieces of the same length. How long is each piece?
1.hint: Share the length into equal parts. Which number times 4 makes 36?
1.why: 4 pieces of 9 cm each: 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 = 36, so each piece is 9 cm long.

1.q: Mei Ling has six number cards: 7, 12, 18, 25, 30 and 41. Exactly three of the cards add up to 62. What is the biggest of those three cards?
1.hint: Pick one card, then ask which two other cards would make the total.
1.why: 7 + 25 + 30 = 62. The three cards are 7, 25 and 30, so the biggest is 30.

1.q: A bathroom wall is covered with 5 rows of 9 square tiles. Blue tiles and white tiles take turns along every row and every column, and the tile in the top left corner is blue. How many blue tiles are on the wall?
1.hint: Count all the tiles first. Blue and white tiles take turns.
1.why: There are 5 × 9 = 45 tiles. Blue and white take turns and the first tile is blue, so there is one more blue tile than white tiles. 45 + 1 = 46, and 46 ÷ 2 = 23 tiles.

1.q: Ravi has four number cards: 6, 2, 8 and 4. He uses two of them to make the biggest 2-digit number he can. What number does he make?
1.hint: The biggest digit should go in the tens place.
1.why: Put the biggest card, 8, in the tens place and the next biggest card, 6, in the ones place. The number is 86.

1.q: A table shows how many pupils took the MRT to school: Monday 14, Tuesday 8, Wednesday 16 and Thursday 12. How many pupils took the MRT on these four days altogether?
1.hint: Add two numbers first, then add the next number.

1.q: Zara has 100 stickers. 35 of them go to Ravi and 28 of them go to Mei. How many are left for Zara?
1.hint: Find how many stickers she gave away in all. Then take that from what she had.
1.why: Given away: 35 + 28 = 63. Left: 100 − 63 = 37 stickers.

1.q: Wei Jie writes all the numbers from 1 to 50. How many of the numbers have the digit 3 in them? (3, 13 and 35 are some of them.)
1.hint: Count the numbers with 3 in the ones place. Then count the numbers with 3 in the tens place. Take care with 33.
1.why: Ones digit 3: 3, 13, 23, 33, 43, which is 5 numbers. Tens digit 3: 30 to 39, which is 10 numbers. 33 is in both lists, so 5 + 10 − 1 = 14 numbers.

1.q: 28 children queue for the school bus. Dina is 5th from the front. Counting from the back, which place is she in?
1.hint: Draw a dot for each child. Mark Dina's dot and count the dots behind her.
1.why: 4 children stand in front of Dina, so 28 − 4 = 24 children are from Dina to the back. She is 24th from the back.

1.q: Tara's holiday lasts 2 weeks and 3 days. Raj's holiday lasts 12 days. How many days longer is Tara's holiday?
1.hint: There are 7 days in a week. Change Tara's weeks into days first.
1.why: A week has 7 days, so 2 weeks are 7 + 7 = 14 days. With 3 more days, Tara's holiday is 14 + 3 = 17 days long. 17 − 12 = 5 days.

1.q: Ben draws 7 marks on a long paper strip. The marks are the same distance apart. The first mark says 15 and the last mark says 75. What does mark number 5 say?
1.hint: Count the gaps between the marks, not the marks. Then find how much one gap is worth.
1.why: 7 marks make 6 gaps. From 15 to 75 is 75 − 15 = 60, so one gap is 60 ÷ 6 = 10. Mark number 5 is 4 gaps from the first mark: 15 + 4 × 10 = 55.

1.q: It is 20 minutes past 4. Mum says the bus will come in 35 minutes. When the bus comes, the minute hand points to which number on the clock?
1.hint: Each number on the clock face is 5 minutes. Find the minutes past the hour first.
1.why: 20 + 35 = 55 minutes past 4. The minute hand points to the number 55 ÷ 5 = 11.

1.q: 44 children enter a marbles contest. Every game is between 2 children and the loser is out. If an odd number of children are left in a round, one child waits for the next round. How many games are played until one winner is left?
1.hint: Each game sends exactly one child out. How many children must go out?
1.why: Only 1 winner is left, so 43 children must be knocked out. Each game knocks out 1 child, so the contest needs 43 games.

1.q: In a sign graph, each bicycle sign stands for 10 bicycles. Block A has 8 signs and Block B has 2 signs. How many more bicycles does Block A have than Block B?
1.hint: First find how many more signs Block A has. Then think about what each sign is worth.
1.why: Block A has 6 more signs. Each sign is worth 10 bicycles, so 6 × 10 = 60 bicycles.

1.q: A basket holds 56 apples and pears. There are 12 more apples than pears. How many apples are in the basket?
1.hint: If there were the same number of apples and pears, each would be half of the total. Take away the extra apples first.
1.why: Take away the 12 extra apples: 56 − 12 = 44. The rest is shared equally between apples and pears, so there are 44 ÷ 2 = 22 pears. The apples are 22 + 12 = 34 apples.

1.q: Jin makes house numbers out of matchsticks. The table shows how many matchsticks each digit needs. Jin makes every house number from 41 to 45, one after another. How many matchsticks does he use altogether?
1.hint: Count the sticks in the first digit of every number. Then count the sticks in all the second digits.
1.why: The first digit is 4 in all 5 numbers: 5 × 4 = 20 sticks. The second digits are 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, which use 2 + 5 + 5 + 4 + 5 = 21 sticks. 20 + 21 = 41 matchsticks.

1.q: A cinema has 9 seats in every row. Tickets give each seat a number, counting 1, 2, 3 and on, one row after another, starting at the screen. Kai sits in the 4th row, in the 5th seat from the left. What is his seat number?
1.hint: Count the seats in the full rows before Kai's row first.
1.why: There are 3 full rows before Kai's row: 3 × 9 = 27 seats. Kai is the 5th seat in his row: 27 + 5 = 32.

1.q: A woodpecker taps a tree 4 times. The taps are evenly spaced, and it takes 6 seconds from the first tap to the last tap. How many seconds from the first tap to the last tap would 12 taps take?
1.hint: Count the gaps between the taps, not the taps. How many gaps are there between 4 taps?
1.why: 4 taps have 3 gaps. 6 ÷ 3 = 2 seconds for one gap. 12 taps have 11 gaps: 11 × 2 = 22 seconds.

1.q: On Monday there are 5 ants on the window sill. Every day the number of ants doubles. How many ants are there on Thursday?
1.hint: Doubling means two times as many. Write the number for each day.
1.why: Monday 5, then doubling each day: 5, 10, 20, 40. On Thursday there are 40 ants.

1.q: A jar holds 29 sweets. Kai and Lin take turns to eat 1, 2, 3 or 4 sweets. Whoever eats the last sweet wins a toy. Kai goes first. How many sweets should Kai eat first so that he can always win?
1.hint: Try to leave a number in the 5 times table for Lin. Then keep making 5 in every round.
1.why: Kai eats 4 sweets sweets and leaves 25, which is in the 5 times table. Whatever Lin eats, Kai eats enough to make 5 sweets in that round. So Kai eats the last sweet.

1.q: A baker puts 24 buns into two bags, with at least 1 bun in each bag. The bags look the same, so 5 and 19 is the same split as 19 and 5. How many different splits are there?
1.hint: List the splits from the smallest bag: 1 and 23, then 2 and 22. Stop when the two numbers meet.
1.why: The smaller bag can hold 1, 2, 3 and so on up to 12 buns. When it holds 12, the other bag holds 12 too. That makes 12 splits in all.

1.q: Four stalls at the night market open at 6 am, 11 am, 4 pm and 2 pm. Which opening time is the latest in the day?
1.hint: Times with pm come after times with am in the same day.
1.why: The am times are in the morning and the pm times are in the afternoon. Of 4 pm and 2 pm, the later one is 4 pm.

1.q: A drinks machine takes only 20-cent and 50-cent coins and gives no change. Its prices go 10 cents, 20 cents, 30 cents and so on, up to 150 cents. That is 15 prices. How many of the 15 prices can be paid exactly?
1.hint: Find the prices that cannot be paid. Start with the small prices.
1.why: 10 cents and 30 cents cannot be paid. All the others can, for example 40 = 20 + 20, 70 = 20 + 50 and 90 = 20 + 20 + 50. That is 15 − 2 = 13 prices.

1.q: A picnic at East Coast Park starts at 10 o'clock in the morning. It lasts 4 hours. At what o'clock does the picnic end?
1.hint: Count on the hours on a clock face. After 12 comes 1.
1.why: Count on from 10 o'clock: 11, 12, 1, 2. The picnic ends at 2 o'clock.

2.q: Aisha borrows a book on 25 October. It is due 17 days later, in the next month. On which day of the next month is it due?
2.hint: Count how many days are left in the month she borrows it. Then count the rest into the next month.
2.why: October has 31 days. From 25 October, 31 − 25 = 6 days take her to the end of the month. The other 17 − 6 = 11 days are in the next month, so the book is due on day 11.

2.q: The school hall is booked on days 8 to 45 of the term for the chess club and on days 30 to 62 for the drama club. Both clubs have the first and last day of their booking. On how many days is the hall booked by both clubs?
2.hint: Find the first day when both clubs have the hall, and the last day when both have it.
2.why: Both clubs have the hall from day 30 to day 45. That is 45 − 30 + 1 = 16 days.

2.q: At a school fair, a sticker pack has one animal sticker, one flower sticker and one star sticker. There are 5 animal stickers, 2 flower stickers and 4 star stickers to choose from. How many different sticker packs can you make?
2.hint: Choose the animal sticker and the flower sticker first. How many pairs is that? Then add the star sticker.
2.why: 5 animal stickers × 2 flower stickers = 10 pairs. Each pair can go with 4 star stickers, so 10 × 4 = 40 packs.

2.q: A bus comes to the stop every 25 minutes, and the first one comes at 6:00 in the morning. Mei Lin arrives at 8:07. How long is her wait for the next bus, in minutes?
2.hint: List the bus times: 6:00, 6:25, 6:50 and so on. Which is the first one after 8:07?
2.why: The buses leave at 6:00, 6:25, 6:50, 7:15, 7:40, 8:05, 8:30. The 8:05 bus has gone, so she takes the 8:30 bus. From 8:07 to 8:30 is 23 minutes.

2.q: Hana writes the number 482. She swaps the hundreds digit and the ones digit to make a new number. What is the difference between the two numbers?
2.hint: Make the new number first. Then subtract the smaller number from the bigger one.
2.why: Swapping the hundreds digit 4 and the ones digit 2 makes 284. The difference is 482 − 284 = 198.

2.q: A secret 3-digit number has three clues. Its digits add up to 13. Its hundreds digit is twice its units digit. Its tens digit is 1 more than its units digit. What is the secret number?
2.hint: Call the units digit u. Write the hundreds digit and the tens digit using u.
2.why: If the units digit is 3, the tens digit is 4 and the hundreds digit is 6. The digits add up to 6 + 4 + 3 = 13. The number is 643.

2.q: A rectangle is made of square tiles in 7 rows, with 11 tiles in each row. Dina paints only the tiles that touch the edge of the rectangle. How many tiles does she paint?
2.hint: Count the tiles along the top and bottom rows first. Then the tiles at the ends of the middle rows.
2.why: The top and bottom rows have 11 tiles each: 2 × 11 = 22. The other 7 − 2 = 5 rows each have 2 painted tiles at the ends: 5 × 2 = 10. In all, 22 + 10 = 32 tiles.

2.q: In a graph, each book sign stands for 20 books. Class A has 9 signs and Class B has 4 signs. How many more books does Class A have than Class B?
2.hint: First find how many more signs Class A has. Then think about what each sign is worth.
2.why: Class A has 5 more signs. Each sign is worth 20 books, so 5 × 20 = 100 books.

2.q: A school library has 500 books on its shelves. 215 books are borrowed in the morning and 140 books are borrowed in the afternoon. How many books are not borrowed?
2.hint: Add the books borrowed at the two times first. Then take the total from 500.
2.why: Borrowed: 215 + 140 = 355. Not borrowed: 500 − 355 = 145 books.

2.q: Siti thinks of a number. She divides it by 4 and gets 9, with 3 left over. What number did Siti think of?
2.hint: The number is made of full groups of 4, and then the ones that are left over.
2.why: 9 groups of 4 is 9 × 4 = 36. Add the 3 left over: 36 + 3 = 39.

2.q: A garden is divided into 12 equal beds. Dad plants flowers in 4 beds and vegetables in 3 beds. What fraction of the whole garden is not planted?
2.hint: Add the beds that are planted. Take that from the total. Then write the beds left over the total number of beds.
2.why: Planted: 4 + 3 = 7 beds. Not planted: 12 − 7 = 5 beds out of 12, which is 5/12 of the garden.

2.q: A theatre has 12 seats in every row. Seats are numbered 1, 2, 3 and on, one row after another, from the stage. Which row has seat number 480?
2.hint: Divide the seat number by the number of seats in a row. Take care with the remainder.
2.why: 39 full rows hold 39 × 12 = 468 seats. Seat 480 comes after them, so it is in row 39 + 1 = 40.

2.q: Five number cards lie in a row: 4  2  5  1  3. You may only swap two cards that are next to each other. What is the fewest number of swaps that puts the cards in order, from 1 to 5?
2.hint: Look for pairs where a bigger card is to the left of a smaller card. A swap of two neighbours can fix only one such pair.
2.why: The pairs the wrong way round are 4 and 2, 4 and 1, 4 and 3, 2 and 1, 5 and 1, and 5 and 3. One swap of neighbours fixes exactly one pair, so 6 swaps are needed.

2.q: Priya has six number cards: 14, 23, 31, 38, 45 and 52. Only one set of three cards adds up to 135. What is the smallest card in that set?
2.hint: Start with the biggest card, and ask which two cards would be needed to reach the total.
2.why: 38 + 45 + 52 = 135. The three cards are 38, 45 and 52, so the smallest is 38.

2.q: Ali, Ben and Chen save money. Ben saves $12 more than Ali. Chen saves $18 more than Ali. Together they save $96. How much does Ali save?
2.hint: Take away the extra money first. What is left is three equal shares.
2.why: The extras are $12 + $18 = $30. Without them the total is $96 − $30 = $66, shared by 3 equal savers: $66 ÷ 3 = $22.

2.q: At a school fair, the stalls take only $2 notes and $5 notes and never give change. The prices at one stall are $1, $2, $3 and so on, up to $30. How many of these 30 prices can be paid exactly?
2.hint: Find the prices that cannot be paid. Try the smallest prices first.
2.why: Only $1 and $3 cannot be paid. Every other price can be, for example $4 = $2 + $2, $6 = $2 + $2 + $2 and $7 = $5 + $2. That is 30 − 2 = 28 prices.

2.q: Mr Tan saws a long plank into 5 equal pieces. Every cut takes the same time, and the sawing takes 20 minutes in all. How many minutes would it take to saw another plank like it into 7 equal pieces?
2.hint: Count the cuts, not the pieces. How many cuts make 5 pieces?
2.why: 5 pieces need 4 cuts. 20 ÷ 4 = 5 minutes for one cut. 7 pieces need 6 cuts: 6 × 5 = 30 minutes.

2.q: Four friends have saved $47, $128, $85 and $63. How much more has the friend with the most saved than the friend with the least?
2.hint: Find the biggest amount and the smallest amount first.
2.why: The most is $128 and the least is $47. $128 − $47 = $81.

2.q: A film lasts 3 hours and 40 minutes. How many minutes is that?
2.hint: One hour is 60 minutes. Change the hours to minutes first.
2.why: 3 hours is 180 minutes. 180 + 40 = 220 minutes.

2.q: A delivery robot is at the top-left corner of a block grid. It moves only 4 blocks right and 3 blocks down, in any order, to reach the bottom-right corner. How many different routes can it take?
2.hint: Count the routes to each corner of the grid, starting next to the start.
2.why: Add the routes from the left and from above at every corner. The bottom-right corner gets 35 routes.

2.q: 9 children must cross a lake in a canoe that holds at most 3 people. The canoe cannot move by itself, so at least one child must paddle it every time. How many crossings does the canoe make in all, counting the trips back as well as the trips across?
2.hint: One child must paddle the canoe back after every crossing except the last one. How many children can one trip across and one trip back move for good?
2.why: Each trip across and back moves 3 − 1 = 2 children across for good, because one child paddles back. The last crossing carries 3 children and needs no trip back. So 9 − 3 = 6 children must be moved by round trips: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 round trips, which is 6 crossings. The last crossing makes it 7 crossings.

2.q: Hana has five digit cards: 6, 0, 3, 8 and 5. She picks three of them and puts them side by side to make the smallest 3-digit number she can. A number cannot begin with 0. What number does she make?
2.hint: The first card cannot be 0. Find the smallest card that can go first, then use the smallest cards that are left.
2.why: The smallest card that can go first is 3. Then the smallest card left is 0, and the next smallest is 5. The number is 305.

2.q: Mrs Lim's piano class is from 1:50 to 3:15. How long is the class, in minutes?
2.hint: Split the time at 2:00 and at 3:00. Add up the three parts.
2.why: 1:50 to 2:00 is 10 minutes. 2:00 to 3:00 is 60 minutes. 3:00 to 3:15 is 15 minutes. 10 + 60 + 15 = 85 minutes.

2.q: Dina is in 14th place in a cycling race with 28 riders. She passes 5 riders. Then 3 riders pass her. Then she passes 4 more riders. How many riders are behind her now?
2.hint: Do the three moves one at a time. Passing a rider makes Dina's place number smaller. Being passed makes it bigger.
2.why: Passing 5 riders: 14 − 5 = 9. Being passed by 3 riders: 9 + 3 = 12. Passing 4 more riders: 12 − 4 = 8. Dina is in 8th place, so 28 − 8 = 20 riders riders are behind her.

2.q: In one month, the 1st is a Thursday. What is the date of the 4th Sunday in that month?
2.hint: Find the first Sunday of the month. Then add 7 for each next one.
2.why: The first Sunday is the 4th. Adding 7 each time gives the 11th, 18th and 25th. The 4th Sunday is the 25th.

2.q: Mei writes the numbers from 1 to 12 in words: one, two, three and so on. Then she puts the words in dictionary order, like the words in a dictionary. Which number is in 5th place?
2.hint: Write all the number words. Look at the first letter of each word, then at the second letter if two words start the same.
2.why: In dictionary order the words are eight, eleven, five, four, nine, one, seven, six, ten, three, twelve, two. The 5th word is nine, which is the number 9.

2.q: 9 friends are in a table-tennis club. Each friend plays one game against every other friend. How many games are played?
2.hint: Call the friends A, B, C and so on. A plays 8 games. How many new games does B play?
2.why: A plays 8 games. B has 7 new games, C has 6, D has 5 and so on. 8 + 7 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 36 games.

2.q: A ladder has 9 rungs, and the rungs are the same distance apart. The first rung is 20 cm above the ground and the last rung is 100 cm above the ground. How many centimetres above the ground is rung number 5?
2.hint: Count the gaps between the rungs, not the rungs. Then find how many centimetres one gap is worth.
2.why: 9 rungs make 8 gaps. From 20 to 100 is 100 − 20 = 80 cm, so one gap is 80 ÷ 8 = 10 cm. Rung number 5 is 4 gaps above the first rung: 20 + 4 × 10 = 60 cm.

2.q: 10 lanterns hang in a ring, numbered 1 to 10 going round. Mei counts round the ring starting at lantern 1, and she switches off every 2nd lantern that she counts. She carries on round and round and does not count the lanterns that are already off. Which numbered lantern is the last one still on?
2.hint: Write the numbers 1 to 10 in a row. Cross out every second one, carry on from where you stopped, and keep going round.
2.why: The lanterns go off in this order: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 3, 7, 1, 9. The last lantern still on is number 5.

2.q: Kai falls asleep at 10 pm and gets up at 7 am the next day. For how many hours is he asleep?
2.hint: Count the hours from 10 pm to midnight. Then count the hours from midnight to 7 am.
2.why: From 10 pm to midnight is 2 hours. From midnight to 7 am is 7 hours. In all, 2 + 7 = 9 hours.

3.q: Aisha's bus ticket shows a 3-digit number. She likes tickets whose number looks the same when it is read from right to left, like 232. How many such 3-digit numbers are there?
3.hint: Look at the digit on the far left and the digit on the far right. How many choices do you have for the first digit? And for the middle digit?
3.why: The first digit can be 1 to 9 and the last digit must match it. The middle digit can be 0 to 9. 9 × 10 = 90 numbers.

3.q: A playlist has three songs. The first lasts 3 minutes 25 seconds, the second lasts 4 minutes 10 seconds and the third lasts 2 minutes 45 seconds. How many seconds long is the whole playlist?
3.hint: Change each song to seconds first. One minute is 60 seconds.
3.why: 3 min 25 s is 205 s. 4 min 10 s is 250 s. 2 min 45 s is 165 s. 205 + 250 + 165 = 620 seconds.

3.q: A fruit basket holds 4 mangoes weighing 250 g each and 3 papayas weighing 400 g each. Find the combined mass of all the fruit in grams.
3.hint: Work out the mango mass and the papaya mass separately. Then add.

3.q: Aisha buys 6 mangoes for $9.60. How much would 9 mangoes cost at the same price for each?
3.hint: Find the cost of 1 mango first.
3.why: 1 mango costs $1.60. 9 mangoes cost 9 × $1.60 = $14.40.

3.q: A kopitiam sold 450 cups of coffee and tea one morning. It sold 86 more cups of coffee than tea. How many cups of coffee did it sell?
3.hint: Draw two bars. The coffee bar is longer by 86.
3.why: Take away the extra 86: 450 − 86 = 364. Share equally: 364 ÷ 2 = 182 cups of tea. Coffee is 182 + 86 = 268 cups.

3.q: A giant chessboard is painted on a playground. It has 14 rows and 21 columns of squares. Dark and light squares take turns along every row and column, and the top left square is dark. How many dark squares touch the edge of the board?
3.hint: The squares on the edge form a ring round the board. Count how many squares are in the ring, then think about how dark and light take turns.
3.why: The ring has 2 × (14 + 21) − 4 = 66 squares. Dark and light take turns all the way round the ring, and 66 is an even number, so half of them are dark: 66 ÷ 2 = 33 squares.

3.q: Mei Ling climbs 9 steps at the MRT station. Each time she takes 1 step or 2 steps. In how many different ways can she climb all 9 steps?
3.hint: First find the ways for 1 step, 2 steps, 3 steps and 4 steps. Look for a pattern.
3.why: The ways for 1, 2, 3, 4 and so on steps are 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34, 55. Each number is the sum of the two before it. So 9 steps can be climbed in 55 ways.

3.q: A shop has 200 erasers. It makes packs of 17 erasers and fills as many full packs as it can. How many erasers are left over?
3.hint: Count in 17s: 17, 34, 51 ... Stop before you pass 200.
3.why: 11 packs use 11 × 17 = 187 erasers, and 200 − 187 = 13. 13 erasers are left over.

3.q: Mrs Lim puts the same number of eggs on each of 6 trays. She also has 9 loose eggs. She has 75 eggs altogether. How many eggs are on each tray?
3.hint: Work backwards. Take away the loose eggs first. Then share what is left among the trays.
3.why: Take away the loose eggs: 75 − 9 = 66. Share 66 eggs among 6 trays: 66 ÷ 6 = 11 eggs on each tray.

3.q: 36 players enter a badminton knockout. Every match is between 2 players and the loser is out. If a round starts with an odd number of players, one player waits for the next round. How many matches are played in all?
3.hint: Every match sends exactly one player out. How many players must go out for one winner to be left?
3.why: One winner is left, so 35 players must go out. Each match sends 1 player out, so there are 35 matches in all.

3.q: Hana adds all the whole numbers from 1 to 24. She gets 282, but she left out one number by mistake. Which number did she leave out?
3.hint: Work out what the total should be. Pair the numbers: 1 with the biggest, 2 with the next biggest, and so on.
3.why: There are 24 ÷ 2 = 12 pairs, and each pair adds up to 1 + 24 = 25. The total should be 12 × 25 = 300. 300 − 282 = 18.

3.q: A minute hand on a classroom clock starts at the 2 and turns clockwise until it points at the 11. How many right angles has it turned through?
3.hint: A right angle is a quarter turn. The numbers 12, 3, 6 and 9 are a quarter turn apart.
3.why: From 2 to 11 the hand passes 9 numbers. A quarter turn is 3 numbers, so 9 ÷ 3 = 3 right angles.

3.q: Three cards show the fractions 3/4, 5/8 and 2/3. Which fraction lies between the other two?
3.hint: Write each fraction with the same bottom number. The number 24 works for all three.
3.why: 3/4 = 18/24, 5/8 = 15/24 and 2/3 = 16/24. 15/24 is the least and 18/24 is the greatest, so the one between them is 2/3.

3.q: How many edges do a cube and a square pyramid have altogether? A square pyramid has a square base and four triangle faces.
3.hint: Count the edges of each solid separately. Then add.
3.why: Counting separately, a cube has 12 edges and a square pyramid has 8 edges. Altogether that is 20 edges.

3.q: Mei Ling, Ben and Aisha each say one thing about who has the classroom key. Mei Ling says: "Aisha has the key." Ben says: "I do not have the key." Aisha says: "I have the key." Only one of the three children is being truthful. Who has the key?
3.hint: Try each child as the one with the key. Count how many statements are true each time.
3.why: If Mei Ling has the key, only Ben's statement is true. If Ben has it, nobody tells the truth. If Aisha has it, all three statements are true. Only one statement is true when Mei Ling has it, so the answer is Mei Ling.

3.q: Priya is faster than Ben. Ben is faster than Siti. Ravi is faster than Priya. Who finished third?
3.hint: Write the four names in a row from the fastest to the slowest.
3.why: From fastest to slowest: Ravi, Priya, Ben, Siti. The third is Ben.

3.q: Five children read books during the school year. Mei Ling read 24, Ben read 13, Aisha read 49, Ravi read 31 and Siti read 20. How many more books did the child who read the most read than the child who read the least?
3.hint: Find the biggest number and the smallest number first.
3.why: The most is 49 and the least is 13. 49 − 13 = 36 books.

3.q: Five number cards are 48, 61, 35, 29 and 72. Hana puts them in a row, from the smallest digit sum to the biggest digit sum. The digit sum of 52 is 5 + 2 = 7. Which card is third in her row?
3.hint: Work out the digit sum of each card. Then put the sums in order.
3.why: The digit sums are 12 for 48, 7 for 61, 8 for 35, 11 for 29 and 9 for 72. In order they are 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, which belong to 61, 35, 72, 29, 48. The third card is 72.

3.q: On Sunday, Dina reads 3/10 of her story book. On Monday she reads 2/5 of the same book. Give the total as a fraction of the book.
3.hint: Write both fractions with the same bottom number first. Tenths and fifths go together.

3.q: A robot starts at the top-left corner of a grid. It moves only 4 steps right and 2 steps down, in any order, to reach the bottom-right corner. How many different routes can it take?
3.hint: Write each route as a string of R for right and D for down. Look for a way to count them without missing any.
3.why: Each route has 4 R and 2 D in some order. Count the routes to each corner by adding the routes from the left and from above. The bottom-right corner gets 15 routes.

3.q: Mei Ling's evening class starts at 8:35 pm and lasts 1 hour 50 minutes. Write the time when the class ends in 24-hour time, as four digits, like 0915.
3.hint: Change the start time to 24-hour time first: add 12 to the hour for a pm time.
3.why: 8:35 pm is 2035 in 24-hour time. One hour later is 2135. Then 50 more minutes make 2225. The class ends at 2225.

3.q: A pet shop sells only parrots and rabbits. There are 36 animals and 130 legs in all. Parrots have 2 legs each and rabbits have 4 legs each. Find the number of rabbits.
3.hint: Guess a number of rabbits and count the legs. Then adjust your guess.
3.why: If all 36 animals were parrots, there would be 72 legs. There are 130 − 72 = 58 more legs. Each rabbit adds 2 more legs than a parrot, so there are 58 ÷ 2 = 29 rabbits.

3.q: Kuih costs $1.20 each. A cup of teh costs $1.80. Aisha buys 4 kuih and 2 cups of teh. She pays $10. How much change does she get?
3.hint: Find the cost of the kuih, then the cost of the teh. Add them. Then find the change.
3.why: 4 kuih cost $4.80 and 2 cups of teh cost $3.60. Together that is $8.40. $10 − $8.40 = $1.60.

3.q: Three houses next to each other on one side of a road have consecutive numbers, like 21, 22, 23. The three numbers add up to 114. What is the smallest house number?
3.hint: The middle number is the average of the three numbers.
3.why: 114 ÷ 3 = 38 is the middle number. The numbers are 37, 38 and 39. The smallest is 37.

3.q: Fill the 3 by 3 grid with the digits 1 to 9, using each digit one time. Every row, every column and both long diagonals must have the same total. Some digits are already placed, and ? shows an empty square. Which digit belongs in the bottom-right square?
3.hint: Add the top row first. That gives the total for every line.
3.why: The top row is 2 + 9 + 4 = 15, so every line adds to 15. Left column: 2 + 7 + 6, so the bottom-left is 6. Diagonal: 4 + 5 + 6, so the middle is 5. Middle row: 7 + 5 + 3, so the right of the middle row is 3. Right column: 4 + 3 + 8, so the bottom-right is 8.

3.q: Jun Hao draws a grid of small squares, 3 squares across and 3 squares down. He counts every square he can find, big and small. How many squares are there altogether?
3.hint: There are 9 small squares. Now look for bigger squares made of 4 small ones, then the biggest.
3.why: 9 small squares, 4 squares made of 2 by 2 small squares, and 1 big square made of 3 by 3 small squares. 9 + 4 + 1 = 14 squares.

3.q: Two numbers add up to 43. When you multiply them, the answer is 462. What is the smaller of the two numbers?
3.hint: List pairs that add to 43, such as 20 and 23. Multiply each pair. Is the product too big or too small?
3.why: 21 and 22 add up to 43 and multiply to 462. The smaller number is 21.

3.q: A tea shop has 7 boxes with 9 tea bags in each box. 5 tea bags are damaged and thrown away. How many tea bags are left?
3.hint: Use the 9 times table to find how many tea bags there were at first.

3.q: Jun Hao uses lolly sticks to make a grid of small squares that is 4 squares across and 2 squares down. Each side of a small square is one stick. How many sticks does he need?
3.hint: Count the sticks that lie across, row by row. Then count the sticks that stand up.
3.why: Across: 2 + 1 = 3 rows of 4 sticks = 12. Up: 4 + 1 = 5 columns of 2 sticks = 10. 12 + 10 = 22 sticks.

3.q: On a toy display, every digit is made with sticks, as the table shows. Mia shows every number from 31 to 39, one after another. How many sticks does she use altogether?
3.hint: Count the sticks in the tens digit of every number. Then count the sticks in all the ones digits.
3.why: The tens digit is 3 in all 9 numbers: 9 × 5 = 45 sticks. The ones digits are 1 to 9, which use 2 + 5 + 5 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 3 + 7 + 6 = 43 sticks. 45 + 43 = 88 sticks.

4.q: A hall has 20 rows of seats. Row 1 has 15 seats, row 2 has 18 seats, row 3 has 21 seats, and each next row has 3 more seats. Row 20 has 72 seats. How many seats are in all 20 rows?
4.hint: Pair the first row with the last row, the second row with the one before last, and so on.
4.why: Row 1 and row 20 have 15 + 72 = 87 seats. Row 2 and row 19 also add to 87. There are 10 such pairs: 10 × 87 = 870 seats.

4.q: A cleaning robot moves from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner of a grid. It takes 3 steps right and 3 steps down, in any order. The corner after 2 steps right and 1 step down has a locked gate, so the robot cannot use it. How many routes can the robot take?
4.hint: First count all routes with no locked gate. Then take away the routes that go through the locked corner.
4.why: All routes: 20. Routes through the locked corner: 3 ways to get there × 3 ways to go on = 9. 20 − 9 = 11 routes.

4.q: The crowd at a football match was 47,562. What is this number rounded to the nearest thousand?
4.hint: Look at the hundreds digit. Is it 5 or more?
4.why: The hundreds digit is 5, so the thousands go up by one: 47,562 rounds to 48,000.

4.q: Hui Min writes the page numbers from 1 to 200. How many of these numbers have the digit 5 somewhere in them?
4.hint: Count the numbers with a 5 in the ones place, then the tens place. Be careful about 55 and 155.
4.why: Ones digit 5: 20 numbers. Tens digit 5: 50 to 59 and 150 to 159, which is 20 numbers. 55 and 155 are in both lists, so take away 2: 20 + 20 − 2 = 38 numbers.

4.q: A ferry leaves the pier every 35 minutes, and the first ferry leaves at 7:10 in the morning. Zack reaches the pier at 9:13. How long must he wait for the next ferry, in minutes?
4.hint: List the ferry times: 7:10, 7:45, 8:20 and so on. Which is the first one after 9:13?
4.why: The ferries leave at 7:10, 7:45, 8:20, 8:55 and 9:30. The 8:55 ferry has gone, so he takes the 9:30 ferry. From 9:13 to 9:30 is 17 minutes.

4.q: In the number 83,517, how much more is the value of the digit 8 than the value of the digit 5?
4.hint: The 8 is in the ten-thousands place and the 5 is in the hundreds place. Write the value of each.

4.q: A shop rounds every price to the nearest 100 cents. A price that is exactly halfway rounds up. How many different whole-cent prices from 1 cent upwards round to 400 cents?
4.hint: A price rounds to 400 if it is within 50 of 400. Does a price exactly halfway go up or down?
4.why: Prices from 350 cents to 449 cents round to 400 cents, because 350 rounds up to 400 and 450 rounds up to 500. That is 100 prices.

4.q: Siti draws a grid of small squares, 3 squares across and 3 squares down. She counts every rectangle she can find, including squares and big rectangles. How many rectangles are there?
4.hint: Count by width first: how many ways to pick a width of 1, 2 and 3 along one row?
4.why: Along one side, there are 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 ways to pick a width. Down the other side, also 6. 6 × 6 = 36 rectangles.

4.q: Kumar types 7 + 6 × 4 − 9 into a calculator that follows the order of operations. What answer should it show?
4.hint: Do multiplication before addition and subtraction.

4.q: Aisha has read 2/5 of a storybook. She has 15 pages still to read. How many pages does the book have?
4.hint: If she has read 2 out of every 5 parts, how many parts are left?
4.why: 3 of the 5 equal parts are left, and they are 15 pages. 1 part is 5 pages. All 5 parts are 5 × 5 = 25 pages.

4.q: A team has 7 pupils. The coach picks one pupil to be captain, another pupil to be vice-captain and a third pupil to be reporter. In how many different ways can the three jobs be given?
4.hint: Choose the captain first. Then see how many pupils are left for vice-captain.
4.why: 7 choices for captain, then 6 for vice-captain, then 5 for reporter. 7 × 6 × 5 = 210 ways.

4.q: Ben draws every line of symmetry on a square, an oblong rectangle with unequal sides, an equilateral triangle and an isosceles triangle with exactly two equal sides. How many lines does he draw altogether?
4.hint: A square and an equilateral triangle have as many lines of symmetry as they have sides. The rectangle is special.
4.why: Square 4, rectangle 2, equilateral triangle 3, isosceles triangle 1. 4 + 2 + 3 + 1 = 10 lines.

4.q: A recipe needs 2 3/4 cups of flour for a cake and 1 5/8 cups of flour for biscuits. How much flour is needed altogether? Give your answer as a mixed number.
4.hint: Change the fractions so they have the same bottom number.

4.q: A square garden has sides of 15 m. Uncle fences all four sides, except for a 2 m opening where the gate will go. How long is the fence?
4.hint: Find the distance all the way round first. Then take away the gate.

4.q: Ali had some pencils. He gave 12 pencils to his brother. Then he shared all the pencils he had left equally among 5 friends, and each friend got 8 pencils. How many pencils did Ali have at first?
4.hint: Work backwards. Find how many pencils he shared out in all. Then put back the pencils he gave to his brother.
4.why: Shared out: 5 × 8 = 40 pencils. Put back the 12 from his brother: 40 + 12 = 52 pencils.

4.q: Mrs Lim's age is 3 times her son's age. Their ages add up to 64 years. How old is her son?
4.hint: Draw one bar for the son and a bar 3 times as long for his mother. Count the equal parts.
4.why: The son is 1 part and his mother is 3 parts, so there are 4 equal parts. 64 ÷ 4 = 16 years. His mother is 48.

4.q: A jug holds 0.75 L of milk. Ben fills 6 jugs. How many litres of milk is that?
4.hint: Think of 0.75 as three quarters of a litre. Four jugs would make 3 litres.

4.q: A farmer packs 2345 eggs into trays of 6, filling as many trays as he can. How many eggs are left over?
4.hint: Divide 2345 by 6. What is the remainder?
4.why: 390 × 6 = 2340, and 2345 − 2340 = 5. 5 eggs are left over.

4.q: A line graph shows the height of a sunflower at the end of each week: 4 cm, 7 cm, 15 cm, 18 cm and 30 cm. What was the biggest growth in one week?
4.hint: Find how much the plant grew between each pair of neighbouring weeks.
4.why: The growth in each week was 3, 8, 3, 12. The biggest is 12 cm.

4.q: Ben buys 3 story books. Each book costs $12.80. He pays $50. How much change does he get?
4.hint: Work out the cost of 3 books first.

4.q: A pie chart shows the favourite fruit of 240 children. The sector for mango has an angle of 75°. How many children chose mango?
4.hint: The whole circle is 360°. What fraction of the circle is the mango sector?
4.why: 75° out of 360° is 5/24 of the circle. 240 ÷ 24 = 10, and 5 × 10 = 50 children.

4.q: In a school team list of 120 pupils, 70 play football and 65 play basketball. 20 pupils play neither game. How many pupils play both games?
4.hint: Find how many pupils play at least one game. Then add the two teams and compare.
4.why: 100 pupils play at least one game. 70 + 65 = 135, which is 35 more than 100. Those 35 were counted twice, so 35 pupils play both.

4.q: Find the smallest 5-digit number in which the five digits have a sum of 20.
4.hint: Keep the biggest digits at the end, because digits on the left are worth more. The first digit cannot be 0.
4.why: Start with 1 on the left. Then 0 and 1, and use two 9s at the end to reach 20: 1 + 0 + 1 + 9 + 9 = 20. The number is 10,199.

4.q: Each letter stands for a different digit. AB is a 2-digit number and CCB is a 3-digit number. AB × 3 = CCB. What digit is A?
4.hint: Look at the units digit. B × 3 ends in B. Which digit does that?
4.why: B × 3 ends in B only when B is 0 or 5. B = 0 fails, because A0 × 3 never starts with two matching digits. So B = 5, and 75 × 3 = 225 fits CCB. A is 7.

4.q: Mr Tan puts 24 chairs in equal rows for a concert. Every row has the same number of chairs. How many different ways can he arrange them? (1 row of 24 counts as one way.)
4.hint: Find all pairs of numbers that multiply to 24.
4.why: The pairs are 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8, 4 × 6, 6 × 4, 8 × 3, 12 × 2 and 24 × 1. Rows and chairs in a row swap, so there are 8 ways.

4.q: Kumar, Priya, Wei Jie and Siti each say one thing about who has the lost library card. Kumar says: "I do not have it." Priya says: "Siti has it." Wei Jie says: "Siti has it." Siti says: "Wei Jie has it." Exactly one of the four statements is false. Who has the library card?
4.hint: Try each child as the one with the card. Count how many statements are true each time. You need exactly 3 true.
4.why: If Siti has it: Kumar's statement is true, Priya's is true, Wei Jie's is true, and only Siti's is false. That is exactly 3 true. No other child gives exactly 3 true statements. The answer is Siti.

4.q: Priya has 126 chocolates and 84 sweets. She makes identical gift bags. No chocolates or sweets may be left over. What is the most bags she can make?
4.hint: The number of bags must divide 126 and 84 exactly. Try big numbers first.
4.why: Both numbers divide exactly by 42: 126 = 3 × 42 and 84 = 2 × 42. No bigger number divides both. The greatest is 42 bags.

4.q: Four consecutive even numbers add up to 108. What is the smallest of the four numbers?
4.hint: Consecutive even numbers go up by 2: n, n + 2, n + 4, n + 6.
4.why: The four numbers are n, n + 2, n + 4 and n + 6, which add to 4n + 12. 4n + 12 = 108, so 4n = 96 and n = 24.

4.q: At 5 o'clock, what is the smaller angle between a clock's hour hand and its minute hand?
4.hint: The 12 numbers are equally spaced round the clock, and a full turn is 360°. How many degrees is one number?
4.why: A full turn of 360° is shared by 12 numbers, so one number is 30°. At 5 o'clock the minute hand points at 12 and the hour hand at 5. 5 × 30 = 150°.

4.q: Mei Ling uses 1.75 m of ribbon for a gift and 2.6 m of ribbon for a card. How many metres of ribbon does she use altogether?
4.hint: Line up the decimal points before you add.

5.q: A bag holds 100 coins that look the same. One of them is a fake and is a little lighter than the others. A balance scale shows which side is lighter, or that both sides are equal. What is the fewest number of weighings that is certain to find the fake coin?
5.hint: Put the same number of coins on each side. What does the scale tell you if it balances, and what if it tips?
5.why: Each weighing splits the coins into three groups: the left pan, the right pan and the coins left out. Four weighings can handle 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81 coins, which is not enough for 100. Five weighings can handle 243 coins, so 5 weighings are certain to work.

5.q: The population of a town is 3,486,215. What is this number rounded to the nearest hundred thousand?
5.hint: Look at the ten thousands digit to decide whether to round up or down.
5.why: The ten thousands digit is 8, so round up the 4 in the hundred thousands place to 5. The answer is 3,500,000.

5.q: A rope is 3.45 m long. How many centimetres is that?
5.hint: 1 m is 100 cm. Multiplying by 100 moves the decimal point two places.

5.q: A cafe sells 3 kinds of cake, 8 drinks and 4 sizes. A set is one cake, one drink and one size. How many different sets can a customer choose?
5.hint: Pick a cake. How many drink and size choices go with it?

5.q: A restaurant bill comes to $200 without GST. GST adds 9% of that amount. What is the final bill?
5.hint: Find the GST first. Then add it to the bill.

5.q: Uncle buys a crate of oranges for $40 and sells all the oranges for $50. What is his profit as a percentage of the cost price?
5.hint: Find the profit in dollars first. Then write it as a fraction of the cost.

5.q: A model staircase has 60 steps. Step 1 uses 1 block, step 2 uses 2 blocks, step 3 uses 3 blocks, and so on up to step 60. How many blocks are used altogether?
5.hint: Pair step 1 with step 60, step 2 with step 59, and so on.
5.why: Each pair adds to 1 + 60 = 61. There are 30 pairs. 30 × 61 = 1830 blocks.

5.q: A bowl holds 20 pink, 15 green and 12 orange raffle tickets. Hui Min takes tickets from the bowl without looking. How many must she take to be sure of having 7 tickets of the same colour?
5.hint: Think of the unluckiest case: she takes as many tickets as possible without having 7 tickets of any colour.
5.why: The unluckiest case is 6 pink, 6 green and 6 orange tickets, which is 18 tickets. The next ticket must make 7 of one colour, so she must take 18 + 1 = 19 tickets.

5.q: A school has 360 Primary 5 pupils. 35% of them walk to school. How many pupils walk to school?
5.hint: 10% of 360 is 36. Use that to build 35%.

5.q: Mei Ling types 6 × (13 + 8) − 25 into a calculator that follows the order of operations. What answer should it show?
5.hint: Work out the brackets first. Then multiply. Then subtract.
5.why: Brackets first: 13 + 8 = 21. Then 6 × 21 = 126. Then 126 − 25 = 101.

5.q: Siti spends 3/8 of her savings on a gift and still has $50. What were her savings at first?
5.hint: If she spent 3 out of 8 equal parts, how many parts are left?
5.why: 5 of the 8 equal parts are left, and they are $50. One part is $10. All 8 parts are 8 × $10 = $80.

5.q: A fish tank has a length of 60 cm, a width of 40 cm and a height of 30 cm. How many litres of water fit into it? (1 litre = 1000 cm³.)
5.hint: Find the volume in cm³ first. Then change cm³ to litres.

5.q: Kai and Dina live 3,120 m apart on the same road. They walk towards each other, Kai at 80 m a minute and Dina at 76 m a minute. After how many minutes do they meet?
5.hint: Each minute the gap between them closes by Kai's speed plus Dina's speed.
5.why: Each minute they get 156 m closer. 3,120 ÷ 156 = 20 minutes.

5.q: A model house has a rectangular wall, 12 cm wide and 7 cm tall, with a triangular roof on top. The roof has the same base as the wall and is 5 cm tall. Find the combined area of the wall and the roof.
5.hint: Find the area of the rectangle. Then find the area of the triangle. Add them.
5.why: Rectangle: 12 × 7 = 84. Triangle: 12 × 5 ÷ 2 = 30. 84 + 30 = 114 cm².

5.q: A number is a palindrome if its digits are the same when you read them from right to left, like 48384. How many 5-digit palindromes are there?
5.hint: The first digit decides the last digit, and the second digit decides the fourth. Which digits are free to choose?
5.why: The first digit has 9 choices (not 0). The second digit has 10 choices. The middle digit has 10 choices. The other two digits are decided. 9 × 10 × 10 = 900 numbers.

5.q: A box is 6 cm long, 5 cm wide and 4 cm tall. Wei Jie fills it with 1 cm cubes, with no gaps. How many cubes does he need?
5.hint: Find how many cubes fit in the bottom layer. Then count the layers.
5.why: The bottom layer has 6 × 5 = 30 cubes. There are 4 layers. 30 × 4 = 120 cubes.

5.q: Aisha puts $2,000 in a savings account. The bank pays 3% simple interest each year on the $2,000. How much interest does she earn in 4 years?
5.hint: Find the interest for one year first. Simple interest is the same amount every year.
5.why: 3% of $2,000 is $60 for one year. For 4 years: 4 × $60 = $240.

5.q: A frog climbs 7 steps. Each jump goes up 1, 2 or 3 steps. In how many different ways can it climb all 7 steps?
5.hint: Find the ways for 1, 2 and 3 steps first. Each new total uses the three totals just before it.
5.why: Ways for 1 to 7 steps: 1, 2, 4, 7, 13, 24, 44. Each new total comes from adding the three totals before it, so 7 steps can be climbed in 44 ways.

5.q: A rectangular field has a perimeter of 176 m and is 51 m long. How wide is the field?
5.hint: Half of the perimeter is the length plus the width.
5.why: Half of 176 is 88. The width is 88 − 51 = 37 m.

5.q: A triangle has two sides of equal length. The angle between the two equal sides is 40°. How big is each of the other two angles?
5.hint: The three angles of a triangle add up to 180°. The two other angles are equal.

5.q: Two ropes are 84 cm and 126 cm long. Siti cuts both ropes into pieces of the same length, with no rope left over. What is the longest possible length of each piece?
5.hint: The piece length must divide both 84 and 126.
5.why: The common factors of 84 and 126 include 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21 and 42. The longest is 42 cm.

5.q: 8 kg of rice cost $26.40. At the same price for each kilogram, how much do 5 kg of rice cost?
5.hint: Find the cost of 1 kg first.

5.q: Nurul is older than Farhan. Ravi is older than Hui Min. Arjun is older than Nurul. Hui Min is older than Arjun. Who is the middle person in age order?
5.hint: Write the five names in a row from oldest to youngest.
5.why: From oldest to youngest: Ravi, Hui Min, Arjun, Nurul, Farhan. The middle person is Arjun.

5.q: Jun Hao pours 6 litres of water into an empty tank shaped like a cuboid. The base of the tank measures 30 cm by 25 cm. What is the depth of the water, in centimetres? (1 litre = 1000 cm³.)
5.hint: Change the litres into cm³. The volume of water is base area times depth.
5.why: 6 litres = 6000 cm³. The base area is 30 × 25 = 750 cm². 6000 ÷ 750 = 8 cm.

5.q: In a group of 60 pupils, 25 join the choir, 22 join the drama club and 18 join the art club. 9 join the choir and drama, 8 join the choir and art, and 7 join drama and art. 3 pupils join all three. How many pupils join none of the three?
5.hint: Add the three clubs. Pupils who are in two clubs are counted twice, so take them off once. What happens to the pupils who are in all three?
5.why: 25 + 22 + 18 = 65. The pupils in two clubs were counted twice, so take off 9 + 8 + 7 = 24. The pupils in all three were counted 3 times, then taken off 3 times, so add them back: 65 − 24 + 3 = 44. So 44 pupils join at least one club. 60 − 44 = 16 pupils.

5.q: A bus travels at 72 km/h for 2 hours 30 minutes. How far does it travel?
5.hint: Change the time to hours first. 30 minutes is half an hour.
5.why: 2 hours 30 minutes is 2.5 hours. 72 × 2.5 = 180 km.

5.q: A tower is built from cubes in 9 layers. The top layer is 1 cube. Each layer below is a square one cube wider each way: 2 by 2, 3 by 3 and so on, down to the bottom layer. Find the total number of cubes in the tower.
5.hint: Find the number of cubes in each layer: 1, 4, 9 and so on. Then add the layers.
5.why: The layers are 1 + 4 + 9 + 16 + 25 + 36 + 49 + 64 + 81. Added together they make 285 cubes.

5.q: A flask holds 3/4 L of soup. Priya drinks 2/3 of the soup in the flask. How many litres of soup does she drink?
5.hint: "2/3 of 3/4" means 2/3 × 3/4. Multiply the tops and multiply the bottoms, then simplify.
5.why: 2/3 × 3/4 = 6/12, and 6/12 is the same as 1/2. She drinks 1/2 L.

5.q: A piece of card is a rectangle with sides of 18 cm and 15 cm. Mia cuts off two corners. The first cut takes away a right-angled triangle with short sides 6 cm and 5 cm. The second cut takes away a right-angled triangle with short sides 4 cm and 8 cm. How much card is left? Give its area.
5.hint: Find the area of the whole rectangle. Then find the area of each triangle that was cut off.
5.why: The rectangle has an area of 18 × 15 = 270 cm². The triangles have areas of 6 × 5 ÷ 2 = 15 cm² and 4 × 8 ÷ 2 = 16 cm². 270 − 15 − 16 = 239 cm².

5.q: A big cube is made of 4 by 4 by 4 small blocks. It is painted blue outside and then split into its 64 blocks. How many of the blocks have paint on exactly 1 face?
5.hint: Look at one face of the big cube. Which small cubes on it are not on an edge?
5.why: On each face of the big cube, the middle 2 by 2 block of small cubes is not on an edge: 4 cubes. There are 6 faces. 6 × 4 = 24 cubes.

6.q: Two fair dice are rolled. Their numbers are added to get a total. Find the probability of a total of 8, as a fraction in its simplest form.
6.hint: List all the pairs that make 8. There are 36 pairs in all.
6.why: The pairs are (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3) and (6,2): 5 pairs out of 36. The probability is 5/36.

6.q: 6 kg of prawns cost $50.40. Aunty buys 9 kg of prawns at the same price for each kilogram. How much does she pay?
6.hint: Find the price of 1 kg first.

6.q: Mr Lim drives to Malacca at 30 km/h and drives back along the same road at 60 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
6.hint: The answer is not 45 km/h. Try a distance such as 120 km and find the total time.
6.why: For 120 km: going takes 120 ÷ 30 = 4 hours and coming back takes 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours. 240 km in 6 hours is 240 ÷ 6 = 40 km/h.

6.q: Three fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at least 2 heads? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
6.hint: List all 8 outcomes: HHH, HHT, HTH, and so on.
6.why: The outcomes with at least 2 heads are HHH, HHT, HTH and THH: 4 out of 8. The probability is 1/2.

6.q: Jun Hao scored 72, 85, 64, 91 and 88 in five tests. What is his mean mark?
6.hint: Add all the marks. Then divide by how many tests.

6.q: Hui Min covers a strip 8 units long with tiles. Each tile is either 1 unit long or 3 units long. In how many different orders can she lay the tiles to cover the strip exactly?
6.hint: Find the number of ways for strips of length 1, 2, 3, 4 and so on. Each answer builds on earlier ones.
6.why: The ways for lengths 1 to 8 are 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 13. Each is the previous one plus the one three before it. For length 8 there are 13 ways.

6.q: Three numbers each 3 more than the one before add up to 87. What is the smallest of the three numbers?
6.hint: Call the smallest number n. The others are n + 3 and n + 6.

6.q: Siti sends a secret word. Every letter has been moved 5 letters forward in the alphabet (A becomes F, B becomes G, and so on). Her message is RJWQNTS. What is the word?
6.hint: To decode, move every letter 5 letters back. Z comes before A, going back from A you reach V.
6.why: Moving each letter back by 5: R→M, J→E, W→R, Q→L, N→I, T→O, S→N. The word is merlion.

6.q: A cube measuring 6 by 6 by 6 is painted green all over and then cut apart into 216 unit cubes. How many of the unit cubes have no green paint on them?
6.hint: The cubes with no paint are the ones inside. How big is the inner cube?
6.why: Remove the outer layer on every side. The inside is a 4 by 4 by 4 cube. 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 cubes.

6.q: Look at this program. When it finishes, what number does count hold?
6.hint: When i is 1, j goes from 1 to 4. When i is 2, j goes from 2 to 4. Count how many times each time.
6.why: For i = 1, 2, 3, 4 the inner loop runs 4, 3, 2 and 1 times. 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.

6.q: A bicycle lock has a 3-digit code. All three digits are different, the first digit is not 0, and the code is an even number. How many codes are possible?
6.hint: Split the cases by the last digit: 0 or not 0.
6.why: Last digit 0: 9 × 8 = 72 codes. Last digit 2, 4, 6 or 8: 8 choices for the first digit, 8 for the middle digit, so 4 × 8 × 8 = 256. 72 + 256 = 328 codes.

6.q: A freezer is at −9 °C. After a power cut it warms by 30 °C, then it cools by 14 °C, then it warms by 16 °C. What is its final temperature?
6.hint: Draw a number line and move along it for each change.
6.why: The temperatures are −9, 21, 7, 23. The final temperature is 23 °C.

6.q: A regular octagon has 8 corners. A diagonal joins two corners that are not next to each other. How many diagonals does an octagon have?
6.hint: Count all the lines that join two corners. Then take away the sides of the octagon.
6.why: Lines joining any 2 of 8 corners: 8 × 7 ÷ 2 = 28. Take away the 8 sides: 28 − 8 = 20 diagonals.

6.q: Read the program. What number does it say at the end?
6.hint: Follow the program one round at a time. In each round, first ask whether x is even or odd.
6.why: Start with x = 9. Odd: 3 × 9 + 1 = 28. Even: 28 ÷ 2 = 14. Even: 14 ÷ 2 = 7. Odd: 3 × 7 + 1 = 22. Even: 22 ÷ 2 = 11. Odd: 3 × 11 + 1 = 34. After 6 rounds, the program says 34.
6.code:
x = 9
repeat 6 times:
    if x is even:
        x = x / 2
    else:
        x = 3 * x + 1
say x

6.q: What is the smallest whole number that has exactly 6 factors? (The factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3 and 6, so 6 has 4 factors.)
6.hint: Try some small numbers and list their factors. Which numbers could have 6 factors?
6.why: The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. That is 6 factors. No smaller number has exactly 6 factors, so the answer is 12.

6.q: Think of a number x. Six times x, take away 10, gives the same answer as two times x, plus 62. What is x?
6.hint: Write it as 6x − 10 = 2x + 62. Get all the x terms on one side.
6.why: 6x − 10 = 2x + 62. Subtract 2x from both sides: 4x − 10 = 62. Add 10: 4x = 72. So x = 18.

6.q: A water barrel shaped like a cuboid is 80 cm long, 50 cm wide and 45 cm high. How many litres of water does it hold when it is full? (1 litre = 1000 cm³.)
6.hint: Find the volume in cm³ first. Then change cm³ to litres.

6.q: How many prime numbers are there between 100 and 200? (A prime is a number above 1 whose only factors are 1 and itself.)
6.hint: Cross out the even numbers and the multiples of 3, 5, 7, 11 and 13. What is left?

6.q: Find the value of 4a + 3b − 5 when a = 6 and b = 4.
6.hint: Replace a and b with their values. Do the multiplications before the adding and subtracting.

6.q: Each letter stands for a different digit. ABCD is a 4-digit number and DCBA is the same digits in reverse. ABCD × 4 = DCBA. What digit is B?
6.hint: ABCD × 4 is still a 4-digit number, so A is small. A must be even, because DCBA ends in A, and D × 4 ends in A.
6.why: The only solution is 2178 × 4 = 8712. So A = 2, B = 1, C = 7 and D = 8. B is 1.

6.q: Jun Hao's phone plan costs $7 a month plus $4 for each GB of data. One month his bill is $63. How many GB of data did he use?
6.hint: Take away the fixed charge first. What is left is the cost of the data.
6.why: 63 − 7 = 56. Each GB costs $4, so 56 ÷ 4 = 14 GB.

6.q: Write 210 as a product of prime numbers. What is the sum of the different primes in the product?
6.hint: Divide by the smallest prime that goes in. Keep going until you reach 1.

6.q: Daniel, Xin Yi, Arjun and Nurul each say one thing about who is holding the spare classroom key. Daniel says: "I do not have it." Xin Yi says: "Arjun has it." Arjun says: "Xin Yi does not have it." Nurul says: "Arjun has it." Exactly two of them are telling the truth. Who is holding the key?
6.hint: Try each child as the one holding the key. Count the true statements each time. You need exactly 2.
6.why: If Nurul has the key: Daniel is true, Xin Yi is false, Arjun is true and Nurul is false. That is exactly 2 true. Each other child gives a different number of true statements. The answer is Nurul.

6.q: The number of visitors to a park goes up by 20% in one month. The next month it goes down by 20%. What percentage of the original number is the final number?
6.hint: Pretend there were 100 visitors at the start. Work out the two changes in turn.
6.why: Start at 100. Up 20%: 120. Down 20% of 120 is 24, so 120 − 24 = 96. The final number is 96% of the original, not 100%.

6.q: A box has 6 egg tarts, 4 pineapple tarts and 2 coconut tarts. Mei takes two tarts one after the other without looking, and she does not put any back. What is the probability that both tarts are egg tarts? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
6.hint: For the first tart, there are 6 egg tarts out of 12. How many egg tarts and how many tarts are left for the second?
6.why: First tart egg: 6/12. Then 5 egg tarts out of 11 are left: 5/11. 6/12 × 5/11 = 30/132 = 5/22.

6.q: A box has red and blue counters in the ratio 2 : 3. After 12 more red counters are added, the number of red counters equals the number of blue counters. How many blue counters are there?
6.hint: The red counters are 1 part short of the blue counters. What does the extra 12 fill?
6.why: Blue has 1 more part than red, and adding 12 makes them equal. So 1 part = 12 counters. Blue is 3 parts: 3 × 12 = 36 counters.

6.q: A dragonfly hovers 22 cm above the water of a pond. A fish swims directly below it, 15 cm under the surface of the water. How many centimetres apart are they?
6.hint: The surface of the water is 0. Count the distance above 0 and the distance below 0.
6.why: The dragonfly is 22 cm above 0 and the fish is 15 cm below 0. 22 + 15 = 37 cm.

6.q: Read this program carefully. What number does x hold at the end?
6.hint: Work through the loop one time at a time and write down x each time.
6.why: Start x = 3. After round 1: 3 × 2 − 1 = 5. Round 2: 9. Round 3: 17. Round 4: 33.
6.code:
x = 3
repeat 4 times:
    x = x * 2
    x = x - 1

6.q: A row of 6 switches shows the binary number 101101, where 1 is on and 0 is off. What is this number in ordinary (base 10) numbers?
6.hint: From the right, the place values are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32.
6.why: Place values from the left: 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1. The 1s are at 32, 8, 4 and 1. 32 + 8 + 4 + 1 = 45.

6.q: Mei has 5/8 of a litre of paint. She pours it equally into 4 small tubs. How many litres of paint are in each tub?
6.hint: Dividing by 4 means cutting each part of the paint into 4 smaller parts.
6.why: 5/8 ÷ 4 = 5/8 × 1/4 = 5/32. Each tub has 5/32 of a litre.
